s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of altered mental status and metabolic acidosis in a patient with multiple comorbidities and recent surgery
salient_findings: Severe metabolic acidosis with high anion gap
key_facts: 75-year-old woman with prosthetic hip infection
Recent revision surgery
Chronic kidney disease with baseline creatinine 130-150 μmol/L
Hypertension, type 2 diabetes, heart failure, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and folate deficiency
Home medications included aspirin, bisoprolol, atorvastatin, furosemide, gliclazide, pantoprazole, folic acid, inhaled bronchodilators, and as-needed oxycodone
Intravenous vancomycin and acetaminophen started on admission
Glasgow Coma Scale score of 12
Temperature 36.2°C, blood pressure 145/66 mmHg, pulse 80/min, respiratory rate 24/min, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air
Sodium 142 mmol/L, potassium 3.5 mmol/L, chloride 118 mmol/L, bicarbonate 5 mmol/L
Blood urea nitrogen 8 mmol/L, creatinine 150 μmol/L
Hemoglobin 10.0 g/dL, neutrophils 16.5×10^9/L, platelets 485×10^9/L
Albumin 17 g/L
Arterial blood gas: pH 7.18, pCO2 1.7 kPa, pO2 16.7 kPa, bicarbonate 8.3 mmol/L, base excess –22.7 mmol/L
Corrected anion gap 25 mmol/L

shortlist.label: Lactic acidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has metabolic acidosis with a high anion gap and recent surgery

shortlist.label: Pyroglutamic acidemia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has metabolic acidosis with a high anion gap and is taking acetaminophen

shortlist.label: Uremic acidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has chronic kidney disease and metabolic acidosis

shortlist.label: Severe sepsis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a prosthetic hip infection and altered mental status

shortlist.label: Vancomycin-induced nephrotoxicity
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is taking vancomycin and has a history of chronic kidney disease

raw.rationale: The patient's high anion gap metabolic acidosis with a corrected anion gap of 25 mmol/L, low bicarbonate level, and normal lactate level is suggestive of pyroglutamic acidemia, especially given the patient's history of chronic kidney disease and use of acetaminophen, which can increase the risk of this condition.

rejected.label: Lactic acidosis
rejected.why: Lactic acid level was normal at 0.7 mmol/L, making this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Uremic acidosis
rejected.why: The patient's renal function, although impaired, did not worsen, and the degree of acidosis is not fully explained by the baseline creatinine level

rejected.label: Severe sepsis
rejected.why: While the patient has a prosthetic hip infection, the absence of hypotension and the overall clinical presentation do not strongly support severe sepsis as the primary cause of the metabolic disturbance

rejected.label: Vancomycin-induced nephrotoxicity
rejected.why: The patient's renal function did not significantly deteriorate, and the primary issue appears to be metabolic acidosis rather than a direct consequence of nephrotoxicity
